title: Lester B. Pearson International Student Scholarships
legacy_titles: Lester B. Pearson International Admissions Scholarship
program_type: University merit scholarship awarded at admission, requiring separate school nomination and a separate scholarship application
funding_type: Full tuition + books + incidental fees + full residence support for four years (university-funded, with donor support)
administering_authority: University of Toronto — Enrollment Services manages Pearson Scholarship applications; the Pearson Program Office within the Centre for International Experience (CIE) supports enrolled scholars
implementing_agency: University of Toronto — Enrollment Services (application processing); University Admissions & Outreach and the University Registrar's Office verify participating high schools and receive the OUAC admission application
programme_action: University of Toronto entrance scholarship programme — Lester B. Pearson International Student Scholarships (school-nominated, full-support stream)
description: The Lester B. Pearson International Student Scholarships are the University of Toronto's most prestigious and competitive award for international undergraduate entrants and one of the largest scholarship programmes for international students in Canada. The scholarships are named for Lester B. Pearson, a University of Toronto alumnus, former prime minister of Canada and Nobel Peace Prize laureate. Approximately 37 students are named Pearson Scholars each year, drawn from around the world including international students studying at Canadian high schools; the official award page reports that 188 countries are represented and cites more than $12M in funding in 2024. Applicants cannot apply directly: they must first be nominated by their current secondary school, which may nominate only one student per year, and must then submit both an OUAC admission application to the University of Toronto and a separate Pearson scholarship application.

award_types: Lester B. Pearson International Student Scholarship — full four-year support
Pearson Scholars enrichment and support programme (no monetary value published)
programme_structure.award_types_detail: A single award type covers tuition, books, incidental fees and full residence support for four years, tenable only at the University of Toronto for first-entry, undergraduate programmes. In addition to the monetary support, Pearson Scholars receive enrichment and support programming run by the Pearson Program Office within the Centre for International Experience: Pearson Welcome Events each September (orientation, team building and a welcome reception attended by senior leadership); one-on-one check-in meetings every semester with an assigned advisor on the scholar's campus of study for all four years; the Pearson Peer Mentorship Program, which pairs Year 1 scholars with upper-year Pearson Scholars; the Pearson Faculty Mentorship Program, which matches Year 2 scholars with a University of Toronto Faculty Mentor; enrichment activities on themes such as leadership, career exploration, alumni networking, graduate school applications and entrepreneurship; a Pearson Social Committee of 8–10 scholars that plans monthly social events; and the voluntary Pearson Scholars Professional Development Plan (PDP).
programme_structure.renewal_criteria: The official award page states the scholarships cover tuition, books, incidental fees and full residence support for four years and describes no renewal application, minimum average or continuation condition. The University of Toronto's 2023-24 Annual Report on Student Financial Support describes an annual scholarship value of approximately $85,000 per scholar per year, indicating support is disbursed annually across the four years.
programme_structure.intake: Single annual intake beginning in September (2027 entry for the cycle researched). The scholarship is not available to students beginning post-secondary studies in January. Students already attending post-secondary studies, or beginning post-secondary studies in January 2027 at the University of Toronto or another institution, are ineligible.

application_deadline.deadline_timezone: EST (Eastern Standard Time). The only explicitly stated clock time is 'noon (EST)' on October 9, 2026, which applies to a high school registering to participate in the programme; the student-facing deadlines are published as calendar dates without a stated time.
application_deadline.typical_application_window: July to November. School nomination forms open in early July (access from July 6, 2026) and close October 9, 2026; new schools may register to participate up to noon (EST) October 9, 2026. Students may be nominated before applying to the University of Toronto, but must submit the OUAC admission application by October 16, 2026 and must complete the Pearson scholarship application and submit all required documentation by November 6, 2026.
application_deadline.application_period: For 2027 entry: school nomination July 6 to October 9, 2026; student OUAC admission application to October 16, 2026; Pearson scholarship application and documentation to November 6, 2026.
application_deadline.official_rule: The official award page publishes three exact dates for 2027 entry: 'The deadline to nominate a student is October 9, 2026'; 'The deadline to apply for admission to U of T and be considered for the Pearson Scholarship is October 16, 2026'; and 'The deadline to complete the Pearson International Scholarship application and submit all required documentation is November 6, 2026.' Schools that have not yet participated 'can apply to join the program by noon (EST) October 9th 2026.' Note that these are substantially earlier than the University of Toronto's general 2027 admissions deadline of January 15, 2027 for international applicants, and that the scholarship application can only be completed after the admission application has been submitted and only via a private link issued after school nomination.
application_deadline.deadline_warning: Three separate deadlines apply and all are much earlier than the university's general admissions deadline. An applicant whose school misses the October 9, 2026 nomination deadline cannot be considered at all; an applicant who submits the OUAC application after October 16, 2026 is not considered for the Pearson Scholarship even if admissible under the January 15, 2027 general deadline. Do not rely on the general January 15 deadline.

programme_duration.official_range: Four years of full support (tuition, books, incidental fees and full residence support)
programme_duration.renewal_note: The award page states the scholarships cover the four components 'for four years'. No renewal application, grade threshold or continuation requirement is published. The University of Toronto's 2023-24 Annual Report on Student Financial Support describes an annual scholarship value per scholar, consistent with annual disbursement across four years. The page does not state that support continues beyond four years if a programme requires longer to complete.

funding.scholarship_type: Full four-year merit-based entrance scholarship for international undergraduate students, awarded on school nomination
funding.monthly_amount_note: No monthly stipend or living allowance is published. The award covers tuition, books, incidental fees and full residence support for four years. The University of Toronto's 2023-24 Annual Report on Student Financial Support gives an annual value of approximately $85,000 per scholar per year, 'depending on the student's program of study'; this is a university-published total-coverage figure, not a monthly stipend. The award page itself publishes no dollar value.
funding.travel_amount_note: No travel, airfare or relocation allowance is published for this award.
funding.fully_funded_note: The official award page describes the scholarships as covering 'tuition, books, incidental fees, and full residence support for four years', and the International Students Scholarships page describes them as 'full 4-year scholarships'. The official page does not publish a monetary value, a delivery mechanism for residence support, or any cash living allowance, travel allowance, installation allowance or insurance allowance. No service bond or return-home requirement is published, so the award is not conditional on future service.
funding.program_level_funding_figure: The official award page states '$12M+ funding in 2024' and '37 scholars annually' as programme-level figures. The University of Toronto's 2023-24 Annual Report on Student Financial Support states the university's funding commitment in 2023-24 was about $12.5M, of which $2.8M was from endowment income and divisional contributions and the remainder from operating funds, and that 'Across all year levels, 150 Pearson Scholars each receive an annual scholarship valued at approximately $85,000, depending on the student's program of study.' These are programme figures, not per-award amounts computed by this database.

tuition.conditions: Tuition is covered for four years. Tenable only at the University of Toronto for first-entry, undergraduate programmes. No monetary value is published on the award page; the amount depends on programme, campus and year of study.

book_allowance.conditions: 'Books' are listed as a covered component for four years. The award page does not state whether books are reimbursed, provided as an allowance, or paid directly, nor does it publish a cap.

incidental_fees.conditions: 'Incidental fees' are listed as a covered component for four years. University of Toronto describes incidental fees as non-academic fees contributing to student societies, campus-based services, athletics and recreation facilities and student health and dental plans.

accommodation_support.conditions: 'Full residence support' is listed as a covered component for four years. The award page does not define what full residence support includes, how it is delivered, or whether it covers a meal plan.

visa_support.note: Not published in official source. Eligibility requires the applicant to be a non-Canadian requiring a study permit; a study permit is a condition of entry to Canada but is not an award component. The university's Centre for International Experience provides immigration advising to international students generally.

insurance.note: Not published in official source. International students must enrol in the University Health Insurance Plan (UHIP), which the university describes as a cost separate from tuition and other fees; the award page does not state whether UHIP is covered.

bond.note: No service bond, return-home requirement, minimum grade or continuation condition is published on the official award page. The award therefore carries no obligation that would prevent it being described as unconditionally funded within the four components listed.

total_estimated_value.conditions: University-published figure, not a database computation. The University of Toronto's 2023-24 Annual Report on Student Financial Support states: 'Across all year levels, 150 Pearson Scholars each receive an annual scholarship valued at approximately $85,000, depending on the student's program of study.' The award page itself publishes no monetary value, and no total four-year value is published by any official source read.

coverage: Full residence support for four years
Tenable only at the University of Toronto, for first-entry undergraduate programmes
Enrichment and mentorship programming through the Pearson Program Office (non-monetary)
coverage_limitations: The official award page lists the covered components but publishes no monetary value for the award and no definition of what 'full residence support' includes or how it is delivered.
Exact benefit structure may differ by programme, campus and residence assignment; the annual value published by the university depends on the student's programme of study.

No cash living allowance, travel allowance, installation allowance or insurance allowance is published, and the award page does not state whether the University Health Insurance Plan (UHIP) is covered.
The scholarship is tenable only at the University of Toronto and only for first-entry undergraduate programmes; it is not transferable and cannot be deferred to another institution or a later intake.
If awarded, the scholarship is restricted to the applicant's top choice of programme at the time scholarship decisions are made, even though up to three programme areas may be applied for.
Support is stated for four years; the official page does not state that it continues to degree completion for programmes requiring more than four years.

International applicants cannot receive need-based financial aid from the university: the University of Toronto states it is a publicly funded institution and cannot offer financial aid to international students.
eligible_applicants: International students, defined by the university as non-Canadians requiring a study permit
Students enrolled in the final year of senior secondary school in 2026/2027
Students who graduated from senior secondary school no earlier than June 2026
Students beginning undergraduate studies at the University of Toronto in September 2027
International students studying at Canadian high schools
Students nominated by their current secondary school (one nominee per school per year)
final_year_condition: For this bachelor's award the relevant condition is secondary school completion, not completion of a bachelor's degree. Applicants must be enrolled in the final year of senior secondary school in 2026/2027, or have graduated from senior secondary school no earlier than June 2026. Students already attending post-secondary studies, and students beginning post-secondary studies in January 2027 at the University of Toronto or another post-secondary institution, are not eligible.
equivalent_degree_note: An equivalent prior degree is not accepted: applicants must be entering first-entry undergraduate study directly from senior secondary school, and students already attending post-secondary studies are ineligible. A wide range of equivalent senior-secondary curricula are accepted for admission, including the International Baccalaureate Diploma with English HL or SL, British-patterned education (five IGCSE/GCSE/Ordinary Level subjects plus three A Level/International A Level subjects, with four AS subjects considered for most programmes), six CAPE units, the French Baccalauréat including Anglais, a U.S.-patterned high school diploma from an accredited high school, and national curricula listed in the university's High School Requirements by Country section. The IB Career-related Programme is not accepted as a basis of admission to degree programmes.
previous_award_restriction: None published. The official award page does not bar applicants or recipients from holding, or having held, other scholarships or awards, and publishes no restriction on concurrent awards, funding or sponsorship.

eligibility.citizenship: Must be an international student, which the university defines as a non-Canadian requiring a study permit. International students studying at Canadian high schools are also eligible. No nationality quota is published; the official award page states that 188 countries are represented among Pearson Scholars.
eligibility.residence_requirement: No residence requirement is published beyond being a non-Canadian requiring a study permit. Applicants may attend secondary school anywhere in the world, including in Canada.
eligibility.secondary_school_requirement: Must be enrolled in the final year of senior secondary school in 2026/2027, or have graduated from senior secondary school no earlier than June 2026. Students already attending post-secondary studies, or beginning post-secondary studies in January 2027 at the University of Toronto or another institution, are not eligible.
eligibility.academic_requirements: Must be admissible to a first-entry undergraduate programme at the University of Toronto. No minimum average, GPA or rank is published specifically for the Pearson Scholarship. The university publishes curriculum-specific minimum admission requirements and states that conditional offers will be made on the previous year's grades and in-term or mid-term results where available, with all required documents due by the published document deadline. For U.S.-patterned education the university expects competitive applicants to be enrolled in a rigorous academic course load and to have taken the highest level of course available in prerequisite subjects.
eligibility.gpa_requirement: No GPA, minimum average or class rank is published as a Pearson Scholarship criterion. The university's curriculum-specific minimum admission requirements function as the academic floor for admission, and U of T assesses applicants holistically within their academic context.
eligibility.language_requirement: All applicants must demonstrate a high level of English proficiency unless they qualify for an exemption. Exemptions apply to applicants who have completed or are completing four or more years of full-time study in a recognized Canadian school in Canada, or four or more years of full-time study in an English-language school located in a country where the dominant language is English. Regardless of test results, all applicants must present a senior/Grade 12 English course (equivalent to Ontario ENG4U/EAE4U), which is calculated as part of the admission average. Minimum scores are institution-wide admission requirements, not scholarship-specific thresholds: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 with no band below 6.0; TOEFL iBT overall 4.5 with 4.5 in Writing and 4.0 in Speaking for tests completed on or after January 21, 2026 (or a total of 89 with 22 in each of Speaking and Writing for tests completed before that date); PTE Academic overall 65 with no part below 60; Duolingo English Test overall 120 with 120 in Production for tests completed on or after July 1, 2024; CAEL overall 70 with no part below 60; Cambridge English C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency overall 180 with at least 170 in each component.
eligibility.work_experience: None required. Not a published criterion.
eligibility.extracurricular_requirement: Applicants are expected to be recognised as leaders within their school. The university states that 'a special emphasis is placed on the impact the student has had on the life of their school and community'.
eligibility.leadership_requirement: Yes. The scholarship recognises students who demonstrate exceptional academic achievement, creativity and leadership potential, who are recognised as leaders within their school, and whose future potential to contribute positively to the global community is emphasised.
eligibility.financial_need: Not a stated criterion. The award is merit-based and the official pages publish no financial-need test. Financial need may be relevant to other University of Toronto international admission awards, but not to the Pearson Scholarship. The university states it cannot offer financial aid to international students.
eligibility.enrolment_status_requirement: Must be entering first-entry undergraduate studies at the University of Toronto in September 2027. Students already attending post-secondary studies, and students beginning post-secondary studies in January 2027 at the University of Toronto or another post-secondary institution, are ineligible. Applicants may be nominated by their school before applying to the University of Toronto, but must apply for admission in order to submit the scholarship application.
eligibility.health_requirement: None published for the award itself. International students must enrol in the University Health Insurance Plan (UHIP).
eligibility.field_restrictions: None for the award itself. Applicants may apply to up to three programme areas on the admission application; however, if awarded, the Pearson Scholarship is restricted to the applicant's top choice of programme at the time scholarship decisions are made. Some programme areas require supplemental applications and prerequisites.

academic_requirements.percentage_note: No fixed percentage, minimum admission average, GPA threshold or class rank is published for the Lester B. Pearson International Scholarship on any official University of Toronto page read. Academic assessment is relative to the applicant's curriculum and school context.
academic_requirements.programme_specific_requirements: Applicants must be admissible to a first-entry undergraduate programme. The university sets curriculum-specific minimum requirements, including: International Baccalaureate Diploma with English HL or SL (prerequisites at Standard or Higher Level; final results must be submitted electronically by the IBO); British-patterned education requiring five IGCSE/GCSE/Ordinary Level academic subjects and three A Level/International A Level academic subjects (four AS subjects considered for most programmes), with English required and Mathematics AS or A Level required for programmes with a Calculus prerequisite, and BTEC National, Cambridge Technical and T-Level qualifications not accepted in lieu of AS or A Level subjects; six CAPE units with English at CSEC or CAPE level; French Baccalauréat including Anglais, with Anglais in both the première and terminale years; and a U.S.-patterned high school diploma from an accredited high school with prerequisites at Senior Year/Grade 12 level or AP/IB, and Calculus, AP Calculus (AB or BC) or one semester of university calculus for most mathematics, science, computer science and commerce programmes. Applicants following a national curriculum can consult High School Requirements by Country. Applicants must apply to at least one undergraduate programme, and may apply to up to three programme areas; several programme areas require supplemental applications by their own deadlines.
selection_factors_may_include: Leadership potential and being recognised as a leader within the school
Impact the student has had on the life of their school and community
Future potential to contribute positively to the global community
School nomination as the school's single top candidate
academic_requirements.holistic_selection_note: The official pages describe recognition of 'exceptional academic achievement, creativity and leadership potential', and the University of Toronto Scarborough page states that 'a special emphasis is placed on the impact the student has had on the life of their school and community, and their future potential to contribute positively to the global community.' No published weighting, scoring rubric or ranking of criteria is given, and no interview is described.

english_requirement.minimum_ielts: Overall band 6.5 with no band below 6.0 (IELTS Academic, including IELTS Online). IELTS Indicator and IELTS One Skill Retake results are not accepted.
english_requirement.minimum_toefl: Overall score of 4.5 with 4.5 in Writing and 4.0 in Speaking for tests completed on or after January 21, 2026; for tests completed before January 21, 2026, a total score of 89 with 22 in each of Speaking and Writing. TOEFL iBT including Home Edition and Paper Edition. TOEFL Essentials, TOEFL ITP and TOEFL ITP Plus for China are not accepted, and TOEFL MyBest scores are not used.
english_requirement.minimum_pte: Overall score of 65 with no part below 60 (PTE Academic, including UKVI sittings).
english_requirement.minimum_duolingo: Overall score of 120 with a score of 120 in Production (Duolingo English Test, for tests completed on or after July 1, 2024).
english_requirement.moi_rule: A senior/Grade 12 English course is mandatory for admission to all programmes and is calculated as part of the admission average, but it does not satisfy the English proficiency requirement. Exemption from the proficiency test requires four or more years of full-time study in a recognized Canadian school in Canada, or four or more years of full-time study in an English-language school in a country where the dominant language is English.
english_requirement.test_score_note: These are University of Toronto institution-wide undergraduate admission requirements, not Pearson-specific thresholds. Scores must be sent electronically by the testing agency directly to University Admissions & Outreach; scores submitted by the applicant or their school are not accepted. Do not send results until the U of T applicant number has been received. Register for tests using the same first name, surname and date of birth as on the admission application. Scores are also required by the published supporting-documentation deadline. Applicants who do not meet the requirement but are otherwise admissible may be considered for English Language Transition Programs (six weeks to eight months, offered on all three campuses).
accepted_tests: Cambridge English C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency (minimum overall 180, at least 170 in each component; B2 First not accepted)
Canadian Academic English Language Assessment (CAEL), including CAEL Online (overall 70, no part below 60)
Caribbean Examinations Council English courses (final grade A (I) or B (II) in CSEC English)
Duolingo English Test (overall 120, 120 in Production; tests on or after July 1, 2024)
English Language Diagnosis and Assessment / Certificate of Proficiency in English (ELDA/COPE) (total 86, 32 Writing, 22 each Reading and Listening; discretionary range total 80+)

GCSE/IGCSE/GCE/AICE English (minimum final grade B/6 in Ordinary Level English, English Language or English as a Second Language, or minimum final or predicted grade C in GCE A Level/AS Level/AICE English or English Language; English as an Additional Language and English Literature not accepted)
International Baccalaureate English (at least 4 predicted or final in HL or SL English A: Literature or English A: Language and Literature; IB English B HL with a score of 7 also acceptable)
IELTS Academic, including IELTS Online (overall 6.5, no band below 6.0)
Pearson Test of English (PTE) Academic (overall 65, no part below 60)
TOEFL iBT, including Home Edition and Paper Edition (overall 4.5, 4.5 Writing, 4.0 Speaking for tests on or after January 21, 2026; total 89 with 22 each in Speaking and Writing for earlier tests)
University of Toronto School of Continuing Studies 'Academic English' course (grade B at the 60/Advanced level)
University Studies (one year of full-time study at a recognized university in a country where English is dominant, with at least four full-year transferable courses at grade C or better)
Ontario College of Applied Arts and Technology (three-year Advanced Diploma or final-semester enrolment with overall B+ standing, all study completed in Ontario)

language_of_instruction.language_note: English is the language of instruction and examination at the University of Toronto, and the university states that success in its degree programmes requires a high level of English proficiency. The university publishes French-language admission pathways for the French Baccalauréat (including Anglais in the première and terminale years), but instruction is in English.

application_method.application_route: Two linked applications are required and neither can substitute for the other. First the applicant's current secondary school must nominate them through the university's secure online nomination process (one nominee per school per year; the school receives a personalised nomination form from July, or must first register to participate). Second, the student must submit an undergraduate application through the Ontario Universities' Application Centre (OUAC) to the University of Toronto, then complete the Join U of T (or Engineering Applicant Portal) steps. Only after both nomination and the admission application are in place is the student issued a private link to the Lester B. Pearson International Student Scholarship application, which is submitted together with all required documentation by the published deadline.
application_method.portal_url: https://join.utoronto.ca/ (Join U of T applicant portal); Engineering applicants use https://portal.engineering.utoronto.ca/sites/myportal/ (Engineering Applicant Portal). School-side: https://apply.adm.utoronto.ca/register/pearson-participate (school participation registration). Questions: https://apply.adm.utoronto.ca/register/pearson-inquiry (Pearson Scholarship Inquiry Form).
application_steps: 1. Confirm eligibility: be a non-Canadian requiring a study permit; be in the final year of senior secondary school in 2026/2027 or have graduated no earlier than June 2026; and be beginning studies at the University of Toronto in September 2027.

2. Ask the guidance counsellor, principal or head of school whether the school is eligible to nominate students for the Lester B. Pearson International Student Scholarship. Schools already verified by University Admissions & Outreach and the University Registrar's Office are contacted by email each July with a personalised, secure nomination form; unverified schools must first apply to participate in the programme.

3. School submits the nomination by the nomination deadline (October 9, 2026 for 2027 entry). Each school may nominate only one student per year, and the university encourages the school to nominate the student who best exemplifies the qualities of a Pearson Scholar.
4. Student submits an OUAC undergraduate application to the University of Toronto, selecting up to three programme areas, by the Pearson admission deadline (October 16, 2026 for 2027 entry).

5. About a week after the OUAC application is received, the student receives instructions to log into the Join U of T or Engineering Applicant Portal, where required documents, supplemental applications and next steps are listed.

6. Student completes the Pearson scholarship application using the private link issued after nomination. This can only be done after the admission application has been submitted. The application and all required documentation must be submitted by the scholarship application deadline (November 6, 2026 for 2027 entry).
7. University review and decision. Meeting the English language requirement is a condition of admission.

universal_documents: OUAC undergraduate application to the University of Toronto (all applications start with the Ontario Universities' Application Centre)
Complete documentation (transcripts) for all secondary and post-secondary studies attempted
Proof of English language proficiency, where the applicant is required to present it and does not qualify for an exemption
Pearson scholarship application completed via the private link issued after nomination, with all required documentation
commonly_requested_documents: Standardized test results (for example SAT, ACT, IB, AP)
Mid-term / in-term results where final results are not yet available
Programme-specific supplemental applications and profiles where required
Any further documents listed on the applicant portal for the applicant's academic background
official_application_documents.secondary_school_documents: Full documentation (transcripts) for all secondary studies attempted. Applicants currently studying in an Ontario high school do not upload transcripts: the school sends Grade 11 and 12 results through the OUAC, and unsolicited Ontario transcripts or report cards are not reviewed. Most students apply in their final year of high school, and conditional offers may be made on previous-year grades and in-term or mid-term results. For International Baccalaureate applicants, final results must be submitted electronically by the IBO. For GCE/ British-patterned applicants, final IGCSE/GCSE/O Level and AS/A Level results must be issued by the appropriate examination board.
official_application_documents.document_language: Documents in English or French are accepted. Documents in any other language require notarized translations.
official_application_documents.document_format: Electronic submission is preferred and required wherever available: transcripts and test scores should be sent directly by the school, examination authority or testing agency. Where electronic submission is not available, documents may be uploaded manually on the Join U of T applicant portal or the Engineering Applicant Portal. Uploaded (unofficial) documents may support a provisional admission decision, but official transcripts sent directly by the issuing institution are required at any point and are always required to finalize an offer.
official_application_documents.transcript_requirement: Transcripts are required for all secondary and post-secondary studies attempted. Submit what is available by the deadline, including mid-term and interim results if final results are pending, and check the applicant portal regularly. Any documents submitted become the property of the University of Toronto and are not returned or forwarded.

identity_documents.note: The university reserves the right to require recent, government-issued photo identification for verification purposes, and to share English facility test results with other test providers that have submitted results. Not published as a standing Pearson checklist item.

academic_documents.item: Transcripts for all senior secondary studies attempted
academic_documents.note: Required. Electronic submission by the school is preferred; upload to the applicant portal where electronic submission is not available.

academic_documents.item: Transcripts for any post-secondary studies attempted
academic_documents.note: Required for all post-secondary studies attempted. Note that students already attending post-secondary studies are ineligible for the Pearson Scholarship, though documentation of any attempted studies is still required for the admission application.
Requested where applicable, depending on academic background, through the applicant portal.

academic_documents.item: Standardized test results (SAT, ACT, IB, AP)
academic_documents.note: Submitted where the applicant has written such tests. For U.S.-patterned education, SAT, ACT and AP scores should be sent electronically (SAT and AP institution code 0982; ACT institution code 5366). Applicants to Engineering are required to fully disclose all test scores.

academic_documents.item: Final IB results sent electronically by the IBO
Final GCE / IGCSE / A Level results issued by the examination board
academic_documents.note: Required for British-patterned applicants; predicted results should be sent by the school.

language_documents.item: English proficiency test result (IELTS, TOEFL iBT, PTE Academic, Duolingo English Test, CAEL, Cambridge C1/C2, ELDA/COPE or another accepted qualification)
language_documents.note: Required only if the applicant is not exempt. Exemptions apply after four or more years of full-time study in a recognized Canadian school, or four or more years in an English-language school in a country where English is dominant. Scores must be sent electronically by the testing agency.

Required for all applicants, including those exempt from the proficiency test. Equivalent to Ontario ENG4U/EAE4U; counted in the admission average. Does not by itself satisfy the proficiency requirement.

application_essays.item: Pearson scholarship application content (submitted via the private nomination link)
application_essays.note: The official award page does not enumerate the component documents of the Pearson scholarship application; it states only that the applicant must 'complete the Pearson International Scholarship application and submit all required documentation' by November 6, 2026. The exact list appears once the applicant receives the private link. Generative AI tools are prohibited for creating content for any University of Toronto undergraduate award application.

additional_documents.item: School nomination submitted by the applicant's secondary school
additional_documents.note: The gating requirement. Without a school nomination the applicant cannot receive the private scholarship application link. Each school may nominate only one student per year.

Some programme areas require a supplemental application or profile (for example the Online Student Profile for Applied Science & Engineering, the Rotman Commerce and Computer Science supplementary applications for Arts & Science, the One Idea Supplementary Application for Architecture, Landscape and Design, a Statement of Interest for Kinesiology & Physical Education, the Music Questionnaire, and the U of T Scarborough Supplementary Application Form).

selection_process.decision_maker: University of Toronto. Enrollment Services manages Pearson Scholarship applications and receives questions at pearson.scholarship@utoronto.ca; University Admissions & Outreach and the University Registrar's Office verify participating high schools; the Pearson Program Office within the Centre for International Experience supports enrolled scholars.
selection_process.selection_type: Competitive, school-nominated, holistic merit review with no published weighting or rubric
possible_stages: High school verification by University Admissions & Outreach and the University Registrar's Office
School nomination of one student per year, with the school choosing its top candidate
OUAC admission application to the University of Toronto
Receipt of the private Pearson scholarship application link (only after nomination and after the admission application is submitted)
Submission of the Pearson scholarship application and all required documentation
Holistic review of academic achievement, creativity, leadership and community impact
Award decision and notification to recipients, then to all nominees
selection_process.weighting_note: No universal weighting, points system or scoring rubric is published. The university describes the qualities recognised (exceptional academic achievement, creativity, leadership potential, impact on school and community, and future potential to contribute positively to the global community) but does not publish how they are weighted, and publishes no interview or additional testing stage.
selection_process.results_timing: The official award page states: 'Pearson Scholarship recipients will be notified starting at the end of January 2026. All nominees will be notified of our decisions by April 2026.' Note that this FAQ text references the prior (2026-entry) cycle while the page body publishes 2027-entry deadlines; for the 2027-entry cycle the corresponding window would be expected to run from the end of January 2027 to April 2027, but the official page as read still shows the 2026 dates. Separately, admission decisions for the 2027 intake are released beginning in January and continue through to late May, and may also be released in the summer depending on programme and applicant type.
selection_process.scholarship_rank_note: The university describes the award as its 'most prestigious' and 'most competitive' award for international students and as 'one of the largest scholarship programs for international students in Canada'. Approximately 37 students are named Pearson Scholars each year. For scale, a University of Toronto Mississauga news article on an earlier cohort reported that recipients were chosen from a total of 1,761 applicants.

selection_criteria.additional_factors: Creativity; the impact the student has had on the life of their school and community; and future potential to contribute positively to the global community. Applicants must also have been selected by their school as its single nominee for the year.
selection_criteria.source: https://future.utoronto.ca/pearson-scholarships (award page and 'Pearson Scholars demonstrate exceptional academic achievement, creativity, and potential to contribute positively to the global community'); https://www.utsc.utoronto.ca/artscicoop/lester-b-pearson-international-scholarship ('A special emphasis is placed on the impact the student has had on the life of their school and community, and their future potential to contribute positively to the global community.'); https://www.utoronto.ca/news/learn-more-about-ourselves-and-each-other-u-t-welcomes-its-newest-pearson-scholars (October 2, 2026: 'the scholarship recognizes students who demonstrate exceptional academic achievement, creativity and leadership – and a commitment to making an impact in their communities')

degree_outcome.awarded_qualification: Any first-entry undergraduate degree at the University of Toronto, restricted to the applicant's top choice of programme at the time scholarship decisions are made
degree_outcome.typical_programme_length: Four years of scholarship support. University of Toronto undergraduate degrees are typically four years; some programmes, including engineering, co-op and certain professional programmes, take longer, and the official page states four years of coverage rather than coverage to degree completion.
possible_awards: First-entry undergraduate degree at University of Toronto St. George (downtown Toronto)
First-entry undergraduate degree at University of Toronto Mississauga
First-entry undergraduate degree at University of Toronto Scarborough
degree_outcome.degree_note: The scholarship is tenable only at the University of Toronto for first-entry, undergraduate programmes and is available only to undergraduate degree applicants. Applicants may apply to up to three programme areas, but if awarded the scholarship is restricted to the top choice of programme at the time decisions are made. Pearson Scholars study across the university's three campuses. In addition to the award, scholars receive enrichment and mentorship programming from the Pearson Program Office.
degree_outcome.credit_transfer: The University of Toronto may award transfer credit for A Level and International A Level subjects, International Baccalaureate Higher Level subjects, Advanced Placement examinations, French Baccalauréat subjects, CAPE subjects and other recognised qualifications; applicants should consult the university's Transfer Credit Information. Final IB results must be submitted electronically by the IBO.

student_rights_and_cost_protection.tuition_fee_for_recipients: Tuition is covered by the scholarship for four years. International tuition fee schedules are published by the university's Student Accounts office; the award page itself publishes no rate.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.common_services: Pearson Scholars receive, through the Pearson Program Office within the Centre for International Experience: Pearson Welcome Events each September (a Pearson Orientation, a team-building activity and a Pearson Welcome Reception attended by senior leadership); one-on-one check-in meetings each semester with an advisor assigned on the scholar's campus of study for their four years at the university; the Pearson Peer Mentorship Program pairing Year 1 scholars with upper-year Pearson Scholars; the Pearson Faculty Mentorship Program matching second-year scholars with a University of Toronto Faculty Mentor; enrichment activities on themes such as leadership, career exploration, alumni networking, graduate school applications and entrepreneurship; a Pearson Social Committee of 8-10 scholars planning monthly social events; and the voluntary Pearson Scholars Professional Development Plan. All university students also have access through their incidental fees to libraries and study spaces, health and wellness services, athletics and recreation facilities, academic advising, career services, accessibility support and student-run clubs.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_requirement: None. No service bond, return-home obligation, minimum grade or continuation condition is published for this award.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_breach_consequence: None published. The official award page states no bond or breach consequence. Separately, the university publishes an academic integrity rule specific to award applications: the use of generative artificial intelligence tools such as ChatGPT is prohibited when creating content for any University of Toronto undergraduate award application, and nominees or applicants found to have used generative AI to create content will be disqualified from award eligibility.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm the school is willing and able to nominate, and that it is a verified Pearson participant (if not, the counsellor must apply to participate well before the deadline).
Diarise all three deadlines separately: school nomination, OUAC admission for Pearson consideration, and the Pearson scholarship application with documentation.
Ensure the senior-secondary curriculum satisfies the University of Toronto's minimum admission requirements for the intended programme areas, including the senior/Grade 12 English course.
Confirm English proficiency and book a test early if required, so the score can reach the university by the supporting-documentation deadline; check exemption eligibility first.
Order transcripts and any mid-term or in-term results from the school early, plus notarized translations if documents are not in English or French.
Prepare the admission application and rank programme choices deliberately, since an award would be restricted to the top choice.
Plan for supplemental applications for the chosen programme areas and their own deadlines.
Write all scholarship application content personally; generative AI use is prohibited and disqualifying.

Budget independently of the scholarship for items not published as covered, including books and supplies (the university suggests $1,000–$2,000 per year), health insurance (UHIP) and personal living costs.
programme_comparison_fields: Benefit components covered: tuition, books, incidental fees, full residence support (four years)
Award duration: four years, no published renewal application
Number of awards: approximately 37 per year
Application gate: mandatory school nomination, one nominee per school per year
Application route: OUAC admission application plus a separate private scholarship application
Eligibility: non-Canadian requiring a study permit, final year of senior secondary school or graduated no earlier than June of the preceding year, September entry
Field restriction: unrestricted, but tied to the top-ranked programme choice
Country eligibility: worldwide, with 188 countries represented among scholars

practical_application_data.motivation_letter_strategy: The scholarship application content should be written by the applicant and grounded in their own verifiable record, since the university prohibits the use of generative AI in any undergraduate award application and disqualifies applicants found to have used it. The official criteria signal what to evidence: exceptional academic achievement, creativity, leadership within the school, concrete impact on the life of the school and community, and future potential to contribute positively to the global community. Because each school may nominate only one student, the case must also be the school's single strongest; applicants should give their counsellor evidence early enough to be selected. Because the award would be restricted to the top-ranked programme choice, the statement should connect the applicant's record and ambitions to that first-choice programme specifically, and should demonstrate that the applicant is entering first-entry undergraduate study directly from senior secondary school.
profile_fit_labels: Top of cohort with a rigorous course load in their own curriculum
Demonstrated, documented impact on their school or community
Strong service, entrepreneurship, research, competition or artistic record
Able to be nominated by a school that is a verified Pearson participant
Applying directly from senior secondary school, not from another post-secondary institution
Seeking full financial support to study in Canada, with no other route to fund an international undergraduate degree
common_mistakes: Assuming the general University of Toronto admissions deadline of January 15, 2027 applies — Pearson requires the OUAC application by October 16, 2026.
Waiting for the school to act: nomination closes October 9, 2026, before the admission deadline, and a school that has not participated must register first.
Applying to the scholarship before submitting the admission application — the private link can only be used after the admission application is submitted.
Assuming the scholarship is open to any programme area applied for: if awarded, it is restricted to the top choice of programme at the time decisions are made.
Assuming a prior degree or existing post-secondary study is acceptable — students already attending post-secondary studies are ineligible.
Assuming a January intake is acceptable — students must begin studies in September.

Submitting an English test score that the university cannot accept (for example IELTS Indicator, IELTS One Skill Retake, TOEFL Essentials, TOEFL ITP, or TOEFL MyBest), or submitting scores through the applicant rather than the testing agency.
Assuming the senior/Grade 12 English course satisfies the English proficiency requirement — it does not.
Using generative AI to draft application content, which results in disqualification from award eligibility.
Paying an agent or intermediary: the university states it does not work with recruitment agents or agencies, and fraudulent emails offering application assistance have been reported.
Budgeting as though personal living costs, travel, installation and health insurance are covered — none of these is published as part of the award.

risk_flags.risk: Mandatory school nomination gate. Applicants cannot apply directly; only a verified participating secondary school can nominate them, and each school may nominate only one student per year.
risk_flags.impact: An applicant at a school that is not registered, or that has already used its single nomination on another student, cannot be considered at all regardless of their record.
risk_flags.mitigation: Confirm with the counsellor in early July whether the school is a verified participant and whether the nomination is still available. If the school has not participated, have the counsellor apply to participate as early as possible and well before the noon (EST) October 9, 2026 deadline.

risk_flags.risk: Three separate deadlines, all far earlier than the university's general admissions deadline. For 2027 entry these are October 9 (nomination), October 16 (OUAC admission for Pearson consideration) and November 6, 2026 (scholarship application and documentation), against a general deadline of January 15, 2027.
risk_flags.impact: Applicants who assume the general deadline, or who learn of the award late, miss the cycle entirely.
risk_flags.mitigation: Treat the Pearson deadlines as the only relevant ones and diarise all three. Aim to have the admission application submitted before the nomination deadline so the scholarship link can be used immediately.

risk_flags.risk: Fraudulent agents and fraudulent scholarship emails. The University of Toronto has been alerted to fraudulent emails offering assistance with Pearson applications, and states it does not interact with agencies or educational agents to recruit students or offer scholarships.
risk_flags.impact: Financial loss, submission of false acceptances, and fees paid to unaffiliated third parties.
risk_flags.mitigation: Apply only through the OUAC and the private nomination link issued by the university. Be cautious of any agent providing false acceptances or requiring fees; the university states recipients can only be nominated by their current secondary school through its online process and that the scholarship is available only to undergraduate degree applicants.

risk_flags.risk: Generative AI prohibition in award applications. The university prohibits the use of generative AI tools such as ChatGPT when creating content for any University of Toronto undergraduate award application.
risk_flags.mitigation: Write all scholarship application content personally and do not use generative AI tools to draft, edit or translate it.

risk_flags.risk: Programme restriction on award. Applicants may apply to up to three programme areas, but if awarded, the scholarship is restricted to the top choice of programme at the time decisions are made.
risk_flags.impact: A recipient cannot redirect the scholarship to a second or third choice programme later.
risk_flags.mitigation: Rank programme choices deliberately and verify admission and prerequisite requirements for the first choice before submitting.

risk_flags.risk: Benefit scope is not fully specified. The official page names tuition, books, incidental fees and full residence support but publishes no monetary value, no definition of full residence support, and no statement on meal plans, health insurance, travel, installation or personal living costs.
risk_flags.impact: Budgeting errors and unexpected out-of-pocket costs, even for a fully covered award.
risk_flags.mitigation: Budget independently for items not published as covered. The university suggests $1,000–$2,000 per year for books and school supplies, requires international students to enrol in the University Health Insurance Plan (UHIP) at separate cost, and publishes tuition schedules and residence fees separately.

risk_flags.risk: The official award page mixes current-cycle and prior-cycle content. The body publishes 2027-entry deadlines, while parts of the counsellor FAQ still reference 2026-entry dates (for example 'end of January 2026', 'April 2026', 'July 1, 2025' and 'October 10, 2025').
risk_flags.impact: Dates read out of context can be wrong by a full cycle.
risk_flags.mitigation: Use the 'Important dates and deadlines' block and the numbered steps for the current cycle, and re-verify dates on the live page before relying on them.

risk_flags.risk: Extreme selectivity with only approximately 37 awards per year, on top of the school nomination constraint.
risk_flags.impact: Very low probability of success even for strong, nominated applicants.
risk_flags.mitigation: Treat the award as a reach option and pursue other funding in parallel. Note that the university cannot offer financial aid to international students, and that most other University of Toronto international admission awards are automatic on admission.

unverified_or_removed_claims: UNVERIFIED — 'Funded by the Government of Canada' / 'jointly funded by the Government of Canada'. This premise was carried in the assignment brief but could not be confirmed on any official University of Toronto page read: the award page, the International Students Scholarships page, the Centre for International Experience page and University of Toronto News articles from 2017 and October 2026 all describe the award as a University of Toronto award named for Lester B. Pearson, with no mention of Government of Canada funding. Official University of Toronto sources point the other way: the university's annual alumni news states the awards are 'boosted by donor support', and the University of Toronto 2023-24 Annual Report on Student Financial Support states the university's funding commitment in 2023-24 was about $12.5M, 'of which $2.8M was from endowment income and divisional contributions' with 'the remainder of the funding ... from operating funds.' No Government of Canada funding is therefore asserted anywhere in this record. Note that the connection to the Government of Canada is symbolic rather than financial: the award is named for Lester B. Pearson, a former prime minister of Canada and Nobel Peace Prize laureate who was also a University of Toronto alumnus and served as Chancellor of Victoria University.

UNVERIFIED — any association with the Pearson education company. 'Pearson' in the award name refers to Lester B. Pearson, not to a corporate sponsor; no official source read links the award to the Pearson brand.

NOT VERIFIED — the specific documents required inside the private Pearson scholarship application. The official page states only that applicants must 'complete the Pearson International Scholarship application and submit all required documentation' by November 6, 2026. The document lists recorded in this record are University of Toronto admission requirements, and are explicitly not presented as the private form's requirements.

NOT VERIFIED — a monetary award value on the award page. No dollar figure is published there. The approximately $85,000 annual per-scholar figure comes from the University of Toronto's 2023-24 Annual Report on Student Financial Support and is attributed as such, not presented as an award page figure.

RETRIEVAL LIMITATION — the 2023-24 Annual Report on Student Financial Support is a PDF that exceeded the fetch size limit and could not be downloaded in full. The figures quoted (approximately $85,000 annual value per scholar; approximately $12.5M commitment with $2.8M from endowment income and divisional contributions) were taken from an indexed excerpt of that document and should be re-verified against the source PDF before being published as financial data.

Pearson International Student Scholarships, Canada) is not on the do-not-duplicate list in RESEARCH_PROTOCOL.md and was researched as assigned. IMPORTANT — funding source claim not supported. The assignment brief stated the award is 'administered with the Government of Canada and Pearson, funded by the Government of Canada'. This could not be confirmed on any official University of Toronto page read, and official University of Toronto financial reporting indicates otherwise: the university's 2023-24 Annual Report on Student Financial Support attributes the funding to endowment income, divisional contributions and operating funds, and the university's alumni news describes the awards as 'boosted by donor support'. The Government of Canada connection is nominal, not financial: the award is named for Lester B. Pearson, a former prime minister of Canada, Nobel Peace Prize laureate, University of Toronto alumnus and former Chancellor of Victoria University. No Government of Canada funding is asserted in this record. This is recorded in verification.unverified_or_removed_claims.

VERIFICATION DATE. The schema contract specified 2026-10-03 as the date to use for last_verified_date, _verification_timestamp, logo_verified_at and image_verified_at. The actual research and verification date was 2026-10-10, so the true date is recorded throughout; recording 2026-10-03 would have misstated when the pages were read. The status determination was made against the real date of 2026-10-10: the school nomination deadline of October 9, 2026 had passed, while the student-facing deadlines of October 16 and November 6, 2026 had not, so the cycle is recorded as OPEN.

STATUS RATIONALE. status is OPEN rather than CLOSED because the 2027-entry cycle is still accepting student applications at the time of verification, even though the school-nomination stage closed on October 9, 2026. The general University of Toronto 2027 admissions deadline of January 15, 2027 for international applicants is recorded in the record but is explicitly flagged as not applicable to Pearson consideration, which required the OUAC application by October 16, 2026.

MIXED-CYCLE CONTENT ON THE OFFICIAL PAGE. The award page's main body publishes 2027-entry deadlines, while parts of the counsellor FAQ still reference the 2026-entry cycle ('recipients will be notified starting at the end of January 2026', 'All nominees will be notified of our decisions by April 2026', 'Nominations will be accepted beginning July 1, 2025', 'This year's deadline to nominate a Pearson Scholar is October 10, 2025'). These stale entries are quoted verbatim in results_timing and flagged as a risk; they should not be read as 2027-entry dates.

NUMBER OF SCHOLARS. The official award page states '37 scholars annually' and 'Each year approximately 37 students will be named Pearson Scholars'. Other official University of Toronto sources cite slightly different figures for other years (the 2023-24 Annual Report on Student Financial Support states the programme 'supports 38 international students' in direct-entry programmes and that '150 Pearson Scholars' are supported across all year levels; University of Toronto News reported 36 recipients in 2021 and 37 in the inaugural 2017 cohort). The approximately 37 figure from the current award page is used.

PER-AWARD VALUE. No monetary value is published on the award page. The approximately $85,000 annual per-scholar figure is from the University of Toronto's 2023-24 Annual Report on Student Financial Support and is attributed to that source rather than presented as an award page figure; the same report's approximately $12.5M programme funding figure and its split across endowment income, divisional contributions and operating funds are likewise programme-level figures. No four-year total value is published by any official source read, and none is computed here.

RETRIEVAL LIMITATION. The 2023-24 Annual Report on Student Financial Support PDF exceeded the fetch size limit and could not be downloaded in full; its figures were taken from an indexed excerpt. Re-verify against the source PDF before publishing these as financial data.
